root_cause_of_the_new_blocker.check: S6 section_authoring, the api_reference#types-1 batch task (composition/authoring.py::_type_batches)
root_cause_of_the_new_blocker.method: Zero-provider-call reconstruction: loaded this run's own stored facts.json/investigation.json/dispositions.json/plan.json in the worktree's venv, called the production authoring_tasks() and authoring_schema() directly, and measured each task's real packet+schema size.
root_cause_of_the_new_blocker.measurement: 9 authoring_tasks() sections all produced packet+schema well under 10K approx tokens (opening 3.9K, key_capabilities 5.0K, api_reference-main 7.0K, ...) except api_reference#types-1 (the 32-undocumented-type batch, all 32 fit in one _TYPE_BATCH=40 call): schema alone 66,130 characters, ~5x every other task's total. Isolated why: _type_batches() (authoring.py lines 555-604) builds each type's SectionTask via `SectionTask("api_reference", packet, frozenset(ids), slots, key=...)` with no `slot_facts=` argument - unlike authoring_tasks()'s own main loop (line 742-751), which always passes `slot_facts=slot_facts`. SectionTask.slot_facts therefore defaults to `{}` (authoring.py line 270) for every type-batch task. citable() (lines 649-660) reads `bound = task.slot_facts.get(slot)`, gets None for every one of the 32 slots, and falls back to `task.accepted_ids` - the FULL 32-id batch - as the citable enum for EVERY slot, instead of that one type's own single fact ID. authoring_schema() (lines 607-646) then embeds this 32-entry enum once per prefixItem, 32 times over: an O(n^2) schema, not O(n). The `fact_ids` array itself carries `minItems: 1` and no `maxItems` at all (confirmed by inspecting the built schema directly), so nothing bounds how many of those wrongly-offered 32 identifiers a single type's unit may cite either - each of the 32 units is free to enumerate up to 32 long dotted fact IDs (~40-50 characters each) instead of exactly its own one, which is a direct, concrete mechanism for a completion that can grow far past what 32 one-sentence units should ever need.
root_cause_of_the_new_blocker.counterfactual: Reconstructed the same batch with slot_facts corrected to `{f'type:{fid}': frozenset({fid}) for fid in batch.accepted_ids}` (each type slot bound only to its own fact - the same shape every other section already uses) via dataclasses.replace, never edited into the source file. Schema shrank from 66,130 to 14,360 characters (4.6x) and the first slot's own enum from 1,670 characters/32 entries to 48 characters/1 entry - a direct, measured reduction, not an estimate.
root_cause_of_the_new_blocker.distinct_from_pdfpy_01: This is a different causal stage (S6 section_authoring) and a different mechanism than item 91/PDFPY-01's S10 review.py fold-logic defect. PDFPY-01 is landed and confirmed present in the code (see blocker_reverification above), but this repository never reached S7 in either attempt this run, so PDFPY-01's own fix could not be independently re-exercised live end to end on this repository - it stands verified by code-reading, not yet by a live green run past S6.

proposal.for: the primary/supervisor - needs arrival-list admission before any lane or worker may land it
proposal.proposed_shape: Scope each type-batch slot to its own single fact ID, the same shape authoring_tasks()'s main loop already uses for every other section: in _type_batches, build `slot_facts = {f'type:{fact.id}': frozenset({fact.id}) for fact in batch}` and pass it into the SectionTask (`slot_facts=slot_facts`), so citable() returns exactly one identifier per type slot instead of falling back to the whole batch. Complementary, smaller hardening also proposed: give the `fact_ids` array a `maxItems` in authoring_schema() proportional to the slot's own allowed set size (already true for every section that sets slot_facts; this closes the same gap for the one section that currently does not) so a future omission of slot_facts fails safe (a small, bounded array) rather than reopening this exact O(n^2)/unbounded-citation shape.
proposal.explicitly_not_proposed: NO change to _TYPE_BATCH (40) or to undocumented_types()'s own lack of a cap - that is a different, already-tracked class (tests/components/readme/composition/test_authoring.py's xfail test_undocumented_type_count_grows_sub_linearly_not_proportionally, 'J1'), about the NUMBER of batches on a very large undocumented-type count, not the per-batch schema-enum-scoping defect this proposal targets. NO raise of section_authoring's max_output_tokens (8000) alone - the project's own standing precedent (docs/DECISION_LOG.md, the presentation_planning/source_reconciliation entries) rejects raising an output ceiling as the fix for an unbounded array, for the same reason here: it only moves the observed failure to a larger repository. Needs its own mutation test (a type batch with >1 undocumented type, red before/green after: before the fix every slot's enum contains every other slot's fact id; after, each slot's enum contains only its own) before landing, per loop-prompt.md section 6 rule 14.
